text:
Matty Beniers ended it 55 seconds into overtime, and the goal fit the way Seattle had played all night. Beniers, the No. 2 pick in 2021 out of Michigan, finished a wrist shot off a feed from Brandon Montour to give SEA a 2-1 win over CGY at Climate Pledge Arena. It was a 25% chance by our numbers, far better than anything either side had managed on the night's other goals.

The game was tight and the numbers lean slightly to the home side. We rate chance quality with expected goals, and SEA edged it 2.77 to 2.47. Our simulation, which replays every shot to ask how often each team wins, gave SEA 55% and CGY 45%, so the result matched the play, just barely. CGY took the first goal when Yegor Sharangovich tipped one in at 12:45 of the first, a 6% look. Berkly Catton, the No. 8 pick in 2024, answered in the second on a 5% shot, the least likely goal of the night. Joey Daccord was the quiet difference, saving about 1.5 goals more than his shots deserved (goals saved above expected), while Dustin Wolf at the other end was also good, about three-quarters of a goal above expected. SEA won 31 of 52 faceoffs but gave the puck away 17 times to CGY's 10.

For CGY, there was a milestone in the loss: Morgan Frost picked up his 200th career point with an assist on Sharangovich's goal. Beyond that, the visitors have little to hold onto in this series, having lost three earlier meetings this season by a combined score of 18 to 4 in SEA's favor, including 6-2 in the most recent. That makes this overtime result their closest meeting yet with SEA, and SEA take the win in a game the numbers say they earned, if only narrowly.
